convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in MT5 indicators (iWPR, iADX, iMFI, iStochastic). Simple entry/exit rules with fixed lot sizing. No external .mqh libraries or custom indicators. No grid, martingale, or hedging logic.

long.right: ADX directional difference crosses above zero

short.right: ADX directional difference crosses below zero

params.method: High[1]-StopLossPoints for long, Low[1]+StopLossPoints for short; closes position when trailing stop reaches current price

other_exits: MFI exit: close long when MFI[2] > level (79), close short when MFI[2] < 100 - level (21)
Stochastic exit: close long when Stoch[2] > Stoch[1] AND Stoch[1] < Stoch[0] (Stoch rising then reversing down pattern)
Stochastic exit: close short when Stoch[2] < Stoch[1] AND Stoch[1] > Stoch[0] (Stoch falling then reversing up pattern)
Force session close on Friday close or session end if configured

custom_logic_notes: Entry uses WPR momentum direction (bar[2] vs bar[1] comparison) AND ADX DI+/DI- crossover across zero. Exit uses two independent OR conditions: MFI level breach OR Stochastic 3-bar reversal pattern. WPR entry does NOT use the -20 level input parameter (Ind0Param1) — it only checks rising/falling direction, not absolute levels. Similarly the Stochastic level input (Ind3Param3=20) is declared but never used in the code. Trailing stop logic: for long, trails using High[1]-SL_distance; for short, Low[1]+SL_distance; if trailing stop price reaches current bid/ask, closes the position instead of modifying. isTrailingStop is hardcoded to false and can never be true (line 58+77: isTrailingStop=false then isTrailingStop=isTrailingStop&&Stop_Loss>0 always false). Entry signal uses bars [2] and [1] (previous and current completed bars) for indicators, not bar [0]. Conflicting long+short signals cancel each other (both true = no trade). Order filling type auto-fallback: FOK->IOC->RETURN->FOK on INVALID_FILL error.
python_conversion_notes: 1. WPR (iWPR) returns negative values (0 to -100); the EA compares relative direction between bars, not absolute levels — ensure Python WPR implementation returns same scale. 2. ADX entry uses buffer1(DI+)/buffer2(DI-) difference crossing zero, not ADX main line — must extract DI+ and DI- separately. 3. MFI exit uses VOLUME_TICK — ensure Python MFI uses tick volume equivalent. 4. Stochastic exit uses a 3-bar reversal pattern (MAIN_LINE buffer indices [2],[1],[0]) — not a simple level cross. 5. The isTrailingStop flag is dead code (always false) — trailing stop logic can be omitted in Python conversion unless user enables it. 6. Pip value calculation: digits 4/5 -> 0.0001, digits 2/3 -> 0.01 — this is NOT the standard 5-digit adjustment (0.0001 for both 4 and 5 digit). Note this differs from typical pip=10*point for 5-digit brokers. 7. Session filter defaults to 24/7 (no restriction) — implement as passthrough. 8. Order filling fallback logic (FOK->IOC->RETURN) should be replicated or handled per broker config.
